_comment: Optional overrides. Copy this file to config.json and edit. All fields are optional; delete the ones you don't need. Defaults work out of the box for Microsoft Scout / OpenClaw.
_home: Agent home folder. Default: %USERPROFILE%\.copilot. You can also set the SCOUT_COMPANION_HOME environment variable.
_processNames: Process names of your agent's desktop window, matched as substrings and case-insensitively. These must be the names Windows knows the process by, not the name on the title bar: Microsoft Scout runs as 'scout', so a list containing only 'Microsoft Scout' matches nothing. Setting this replaces the list rather than adding to it, so keep the entries you still need. Avoid short generic words - an earlier version of this file listed 'Copilot', which matched eleven unrelated Windows Copilot processes and no Scout at all.
_windowHints: Fallback window-title substrings, used only when no process name matches.
_labels: Button captions the companion clicks for Allow / Deny inside the agent window. Scout currently shows: Allow, Allow for session, Allow everywhere, Deny. Order matters: the first match wins, so the one-time 'Allow' is preferred.
_askToolNames: Tool names that mean 'the agent is waiting for you to answer something'. These park the turn like an approval does, so the toast surfaces them in its own colour instead of listing them as a step. Add your build's equivalent if it differs.
_activeWindowSeconds: Treat the session as 'working' if its event log changed within this many seconds.
_pollIntervalMs: How often (ms) to poll the event stream and window focus.
_maxSessions: How many concurrently active sessions to follow at once. Each costs one file stat per poll, so this is a guard against pathological session counts rather than a limit anyone should hit. Approvals and questions from any followed session reach the toast.
_sessionRescanMs: How often (ms) to re-resolve which session is active. Between rescans the companion just tails the file it already found, which keeps the poll loop cheap on machines with a long session history. Lower it if you switch sessions constantly and want the toast to follow faster.
_animIntervalMs: Mascot frame interval in ms (80 = 12.5 fps). The mascot moves at the same speed whatever you set; a smaller number just spends more CPU on smoother motion. The animation only runs while the toast is on screen.
_animationEnabled: Whether the mascot animates at all. Also toggleable at runtime from the tray menu or the settings window, which write the change back to this file.
_voiceCommandEnabled: Listen for Hey Scout and type recognized commands into the currently visible Scout conversation. Saved by the Voice control setting.
_voiceReplyEnabled: Read the final answer from the current Scout conversation aloud. Saved independently from voice command input, but it only does anything while voiceCommandEnabled is on - the two together are what make the companion talk. Both default off: voice is opt-in because it takes the microphone, fetches a runtime on first use, and speaks out loud.
_voiceWakeSensitivity: Hey Scout wake-word sensitivity from 0 to 100. Higher accepts more STT variations but can increase false activations.
_voiceNoiseSensitivity: Ambient-noise sensitivity from 0 to 100. Lower blocks more background noise; higher detects quieter speech.
_voiceRuntimeDir: Folder containing the private .NET runtime, speech models, and encrypted speaker profile. Default: %LOCALAPPDATA%\ScoutVoiceAssistant.
_showChatTitle: Which name the toast shows for a conversation. false (default) shows what you asked - the session's own first message or latest request. true shows Scout's own sidebar title for the chat. IMPORTANT: this also decides whether the companion goes looking for those titles on its own, by typing into Scout's chat search - see chatTitleScanMs. With this off it never touches the search box; clicking a session still opens the right chat, and learns the title as a free side effect. Also toggleable from the settings window.
_mascot: Which mascot the toast shows. One of: quokka, cat-white, cat-siamese, cat-calico, cat-black, cat-russian, tuna, shiba, fox, bunny, penguin, armored-pill, ribbon. Also selectable from the settings window, which writes the change back to this file. 'ribbon' is the odd one out: a turning band of light with no face and no laptop.
_opacity: How opaque the toast is, from 0.35 (barely there) to 1.0 (solid). Clamped into that range on load, so a hand-edited 0 cannot leave an invisible window that still swallows clicks. Also adjustable from the settings window, which writes the change back to this file.
_language: UI language. 'auto' follows the Windows display language, falling back through the culture's parent chain (zh-CN finds zh-Hans, pt-PT finds pt) and finally to English. Set a tag from lang/ to pin it: en, ko, ja, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, fr, de, it, es, ru, pt-BR, tr, pl, cs, hu. Worth pinning if your Windows display language and your regional format differ, since auto-detection follows the display language.
_openMatchingSession: Make Open, Answer and the tray land on the chat that raised the prompt, not just whatever Scout was last showing. Scout's chat ids are a different namespace from the session folders on disk and the index that would join them is encrypted, so the chat is found through the sidebar instead: the companion types something the session talked about into the chat search field and takes the freshest row whose timestamp could plausibly be that session. If no row fits, or the window is too narrow for Scout to show a sidebar at all, it just brings the window forward. The sidebar is always put back the way it was found. Set to false to skip all of that and only focus the window.
_chatTitleScanMs: How often to look up Scout's own chat titles, so the toast can call a conversation what you call it. ONLY RUNS WHEN showChatTitle IS TRUE - until 0.8.2 it ran regardless, which meant typing into your chat search to learn a name the toast then did not display. It types each unnamed session's topic into the chat search, reads the row that matches, and clears the box again - no chat is clicked, so nothing navigates. It only ever does this while no Scout window is in front, so you never see it, and it stops entirely once every session has a name or has run out of attempts. Set to 0 to never look.
_chatTitleScanMaxMs: A look that finds nothing doubles the interval, up to this ceiling, dropping back to chatTitleScanMs only when a conversation appears that has not been looked for yet. Losing one - because it was named, or gave up - does not reset it, which it used to: giving up on a session made the scan run more often, the opposite of what giving up should do. Not being able to look because Scout is in front does not count as a fruitless look.
_chatTitleScanTries: How many fruitless looks a conversation gets before it is left alone. Some can never be named: two sessions started inside the same minute cannot be told apart by whole-minute sidebar rows, and without a limit those were retried for as long as the companion ran. A new message to a session buys it one more look rather than a clean slate, so repeated failure still settles.
_startupGreetingSeconds: Show the toast for this many seconds at startup, whatever the visibility rules would otherwise say. Without it, launching the companion has no visible result: the toast hides while Scout has focus, which it does because you just launched something, and Windows files a brand-new tray icon into the hidden overflow flyout. Set to 0 to start silently.
_notifyOnFinish: Raise a tray balloon when a long turn finishes. Measured over three days of real use: 83 turns ran longer than two minutes and 8 longer than ten, and while one of those is going you are looking at another window with no way to know it ended. Only fires when the toast is not already on screen and the agent is not in front - otherwise it would be telling you something you are already looking at. Also in the settings window.
_notifyAfterSeconds: How long a turn has to run before finishing is worth a notification. The median turn is 11 seconds and the 90th percentile 36, so a low value here would fire constantly for work that never left your screen.
_rememberPosition: Put the toast back where you last dragged it, instead of the bottom-right corner. Dropping it within about 16 units of a screen edge lines it up flush against that edge, and it then grows from the edge it is on rather than always downwards - so a toast parked at the bottom stays above the taskbar however tall it gets. Without that it grew down from its top-left corner like any other window: measured at 275 pixels under the taskbar after one session's worth of rows. Edges are taken from the monitor the toast is actually on, so a second screen's taskbar is respected rather than the primary one's. The saved position is checked against the screens that exist when it is restored: an undocked laptop, a display switched off, or a changed resolution falls back to the corner rather than opening the toast somewhere you cannot reach it - it has no taskbar button to retrieve it with. Also toggleable from the settings window, where turning it off forgets the position and returns the toast to the corner.
_windowPosition: Where the toast was last left, in device-independent units. Written for you when you drag it; there is no reason to set these by hand. Both must be present or the position is ignored.
_keepVisibleMultiSession: Keep the toast on screen while Scout is in front, but only while more than one conversation is running. The toast normally hides as soon as Scout has focus, and for a single conversation that is right - it would just be repeating the window you are already looking at. With several it is wrong: Scout shows exactly one of them at a time, so the toast is the only place the others appear, and clicking into Scout to read one made every other conversation disappear. This only holds while at least one of them is still active, so a set of finished conversations does not leave the toast up for ever, and the close button still closes it. Set to false for the old behaviour, where focusing Scout always hides the toast. Also toggleable from the settings window.
_updateCheck: Ask GitHub every so often whether there is a newer release, and say so in the tray. The check runs off the UI thread so a slow or unreachable GitHub never stalls the toast, and it fails silently - being offline is not an error worth reporting. Set to false to never look.
_updateCheckHours: How long to wait between checks. The API call is unauthenticated and therefore rate-limited per IP address; a few times a day is comfortably inside the limit even on a shared connection.
_updateRepo: Which repository to check for releases, and to install from. Change it if you run your own fork.
_autoUpdate: Install a new release as soon as one is found, instead of offering it in the tray menu. Off by default on purpose: this companion's job is to click Allow on security prompts, and replacing it mid-approval would restart it at an unpredictable moment and could drop a prompt that was already on screen. Either way it only ever updates a copy installed by Install.ps1 - a source checkout is left alone, because the installer overwrites its target wholesale and would throw away uncommitted work.
_updateBeta: Also offer releases marked as pre-releases on GitHub, not just finished ones. Off by default, so nothing changes unless you ask for it. Betas and stable releases live in the same list and are ordered properly against each other, so turning this on moves you to a beta only while one is genuinely newer: once the stable release it led to is published, that wins and you come back to the normal ring without doing anything. Turning it off does not downgrade you - you simply stop being offered previews and wait for the next stable release to catch up. Also toggleable from the settings window.
_exitWhenAgentGone: Automatically close the companion shortly after the agent app quits. Pair with Watch-Scout.ps1 (in the Startup folder) to tie the companion's lifetime to Scout: it opens when Scout starts and closes when Scout exits.
_exitGraceSeconds: How long the agent must stay gone before the companion shuts itself down (covers restarts and brief window flaps).
